I am hunting DEAD or LYING UI. Definition:
- A control (button/toggle/form/select) that calls nothing, or calls an action nobody consumes.
- A preference persisted to the DB where NO code anywhere reads that column to change behaviour. Investigate specifically: Domain.autoRenew (is there ANY renewal job/worker sweep that reads it?), Domain.whoisPrivacy (does toggling it actually call the registrar?), SslCertificate.autoRenew (is there a renewal sweep?), Domain.nameservers, Domain.transferEpp.
- Status text/badges that cannot reflect reality (hardcoded, or from a field never updated) — e.g. transferStatus that no code ever polls/updates.
- Success toasts shown unconditionally even when the underlying call failed.
- Progress/"in progress" states that never advance.
- A function computing an honest result that the caller discards for a hardcoded value.
- Links/buttons navigating to routes that 404.

Two known examples that calibrate the bar but must NOT be re-reported: (1) User.autoRechargeEnabled written by lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts but nothing calls that action and no worker reads the columns. (2) A migration action computed an honest outcome and the caller hardcoded status:"DONE".

VERIFY every finding by reading the code. Give ABSOLUTE file:line and a CONCRETE failure scenario. Drop anything you cannot make concrete. Depth beats breadth, do not pad.

Return findings directly as your final message. Do NOT write any file. Also state which parts you checked and found SOLID.

# Audit: domains / SSL / billing / referral — dead & lying UI

Read-only. No files written, no builds, no DB access.

---

## 1. `SslCertificate.autoRenew` — dead preference, and the cert silently dies at 90 days

**The toggle:** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/SslManager.tsx:124-140` (`role="switch"`, column header "Auto-renew & actions" at `:186`) → `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-ssl.ts:121-134` writes `SslCertificate.autoRenew`.

**Every reader of that column, exhaustively:**
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx:30` — copies it into the row for display
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/SslManager.tsx:127,132,137` — paints the switch

That is the complete list. There is **no renewal sweep**. `/opt/nxeon/worker/ssl.ts` exports exactly one handler, `sslIssue`, wired as the one-shot job `SSL_ISSUE` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:787`. The sweep loop at `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:1027-1095` runs billing, product-renewals, game-update, geo, backup-schedule, monitor, abuse, disk-sample — nothing touches `sslCertificate`. No cron route, no systemd timer (`/opt/nxeon/deploy` has only the nightly-scan units).

**Concrete failure:** customer requests a cert on 1 Jan. `/opt/nxeon/worker/ssl.ts:317-329` sets `status:"ACTIVE"`, `expiresAt = now + 90d` (`CERT_LIFETIME_MS`). On 1 April the cert expires. Nothing runs. The dashboard still renders a green pulsing `ACTIVE` dot (`SslManager.tsx:202` → `statusColors.ACTIVE` at `/opt/nxeon/components/ui/primitives.tsx:95`), a green auto-renew switch, and `Expires 2026-04-01` in neutral slate with no warning tone, while every browser shows `NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID`. Toggling the switch off and on again changes nothing either way.

Compounding: `prisma/schema.prisma:901` documents an `EXPIRED` status for certs; `worker/ssl.ts` only ever writes `ISSUING`/`ACTIVE`/`FAILED` (lines 289, 306, 321, 338). Nothing can ever write `EXPIRED`.

Second-order lie in the **real** path: when `ENABLE_REAL_SSL=1`, certbot installs its own systemd renewal timer on the customer VM. So turning our toggle **off** does not stop renewals either — and because `expiresAt` is never refreshed, the dashboard shows a stale/expired date for a certificate that is actually valid. The control is inert in both directions.

---

## 2. `Domain.status = EXPIRED` is never written — a lapsed domain reads "active" forever

`DomainStatus.EXPIRED` exists at `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:189` and is **read** in three places:
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx:35`
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:124`
- `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/domains/page.tsx:116`

Every writer of `Domain.status`, exhaustively: `lib/actions-domains.ts:195, 214, 239, 249, 339`; `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts:231`; `lib/domain-transfer.ts:108, 162`; `worker/billing.ts:297, 523, 559`. Values written: `ACTIVE`, `FAILED`, `PENDING`, `TRANSFER_PENDING`, `TRANSFER_FAILED`. **`EXPIRED` is unreachable.**

**Concrete failure:** customer turns auto-renew off on `example.com` (expiry 2026-01-01). `domainAutoRenewSweep` (`/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:464-471`) filters on `autoRenew: true`, so it never sees the row. On 2026-06-01 the domain is gone at the registrar, but `/dashboard/domains/[id]` renders:
- `StatusDot` green + pulsing, label `active` (`page.tsx:119-126, 177`)
- immediately beside it, a red badge `expired 151 days ago` (`page.tsx:34-41, 188`)
- `active === true` (`page.tsx:60`), so the **entire DNS manager, Quick setup, redirects and the "Renew now" button stay enabled**

`ownedDomain()` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts:389`) and `ownedActiveDomain()` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:72`) both gate only on `status === "ACTIVE"`, so every DNS write is accepted by our UI and then fails with a raw name.com 404 pasted into the error box. And `RenewDomainButton` offers renewal at `domainTermPriceCents(domain.priceCents, ...)` — the normal rate — for a name that is now in registry redemption and costs an $80–100 redemption fee we never quote or charge.

---

## 3. A "needs review" registration spins on `<AutoRefresh/>` forever

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts:246-268`: when `verifyRegistration()` returns `"unknown"` (registrar timed out and is still unreachable), the code deliberately keeps the charge and leaves `status: "PENDING"` with `error: "NEEDS REVIEW — registrar status unconfirmed: …"`.

Nothing ever revisits it. The only worker sweep that touches pending domains is `domainTransferInSweep`, `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:254-256`, whose filter is `{ status: "TRANSFER_PENDING", isTransferIn: true }`. There is no admin action that resolves a `PENDING` registration either.

**Concrete failure:** `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:134` mounts `<AutoRefresh />` for any `PENDING` domain (5-second interval, `/opt/nxeon/components/AutoRefresh.tsx:8`), and `:148-153` renders *"Registration is being processed with the registrar. This page refreshes automatically — it usually completes within a minute."* That page polls every 5 s, indefinitely, on a row that can never change. Meanwhile `domain.error` — the only field carrying "NEEDS REVIEW" — is rendered **only** in the `status === "FAILED"` branch (`page.tsx:141-146`), so the customer is never shown the actual reason. They are charged, the UI insists it will finish "within a minute", and the state machine has no exit.

---

## 4. "Failed registrations are refunded automatically" is contradicted by the branch above

`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainRegisterWizard.tsx:503-506`: *"If registration fails for any reason, you are refunded automatically."*
`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainRegisterWizard.tsx:565-568`: *"Failed registrations are refunded automatically — you're never charged for a name you don't get."*

Both are unconditional, shown before the money moves. But `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains.ts:246-252` refunds **only** on the `not-registered` verdict; the `unknown` verdict (comment at `:246-248` is explicit: *"Refunding here risks giving away a domain we actually paid the registrar for"*) keeps the charge. The engineering decision is right; the pre-purchase copy is a promise the code knowingly does not keep.

---

## 5. `/dashboard/billing` "Bandwidth usage" is a permanently-zero panel

`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:54-66` computes usage from `Server.bwInBytes + Server.bwOutBytes`, and `:228-281` renders a full card: total used / allowance, "% of total allowance", a per-server `MeterBar`, plus two warning branches at `:267` (`Over allowance by X — overage may apply`) and `:272` (`N% used — approaching your plan limit`).

`bwInBytes` / `bwOutBytes` are declared at `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:314-315` with `@default(0)`. Grepping the entire repo for those identifiers returns **five** hits: the billing page above (read), and `/opt/nxeon/worker/abuse.ts:25, 32, 35` (read). **No code anywhere writes either column.**

**Concrete failure:** every customer with any server sees `Bandwidth usage — 0 B / 20 TB · 0% of total allowance` with empty meter bars, on the page whose stated purpose is *"Transfer used this cycle across your servers versus plan allowance."* The two warning branches are unreachable. `/opt/nxeon/worker/abuse.ts:8` even documents the counter as *"updated by the metering sweep"* — that sweep does not exist, so `abuseSweep`'s `deltaBytes` (`:35`) is always 0 and it can never fire either.

---

## 6. Affiliate commission tiers are decoration — the payout is flat

`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/affiliate/page.tsx:132-170` renders a "Commission tiers" card: Starter **$5.00 / referral**, Pro **$8.00 / referral**, Elite **$12.00 / referral**, a live `{earnings.tier.name} tier` badge (`:135`), and progress copy at `:162-169` — *"N more paying referrals to reach the Elite tier ($12.00 / referral)"*.

The numbers come from `AFFILIATE_TIERS` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/affiliate.ts:45-49`). The money actually credited comes from `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-growth.ts:263`:

```ts
const reward = referralRewardCents();
```

…a flat value (`/opt/nxeon/lib/growth.ts:13-16`, default 500) applied identically to both parties at `actions-growth.ts:278-289`. `AFFILIATE_TIERS` is imported by exactly one file — the page above. `currentTier`/`nextTier` feed nothing but text.

**Concrete failure:** a customer grinds to 15 paying referrals, watches the badge flip to `Elite tier` and the row highlight to `$12.00 / referral`, and is credited $5.00 — the same as referral #1. Their next 20 referrals each pay $5.00. `/opt/nxeon/lib/affiliate.ts:38-44` concedes this in a comment ("these tiers are the customer-facing program description"), which makes it an intentional, documented, revenue-relevant misstatement rather than a bug.

---

## 7. Three "saved — will be applied once the domain is active" promises with no applier

Each of these persists intent and tells the customer it will be pushed to the registrar later. Nothing anywhere replays them.

| Control | Writes | Promise shown | Reader |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nameservers | `Domain.nameservers` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:112`) | `:107-109` *"Saved. These will be applied at the registrar once the domain is active and the registrar is configured."* + `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:128-133` | `Domain.nameservers` is read at exactly two places: `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:327` (form prefill) and `/opt/nxeon/app/api/account/export/route.ts:69` |
| URL redirects | `Setting["domain-redirect:{id}"]` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:324-330`) | `:412` *"Saved. This redirect will be applied via name.com URL forwarding once the domain is active and the registrar is connected."* | only `readRedirectIntent` at `:353, 357, 398, 432` — display + local edit |
| Registrar lock | `Setting["domain-lock:{id}"]` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:492-496`) | `:490` *"Saved. This lock preference will be applied at name.com once the domain is active and the registrar is connected."* | only `getRegistrarLock` at `:465` — display |

`grep` for `domain-lock` / `domain-redirect` returns hits **only inside `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`**. Neither `purchaseDomain`'s ACTIVE transition (`lib/actions-domains.ts:195-202`) nor `settleCompletedTransferIn` (`lib/domain-transfer.ts:154-168`) consults any of them.

**Concrete failure:** customer registers `example.com`, opens Advanced while it is still `PENDING`, enters `ns1.digitalocean.com` / `ns2.digitalocean.com`, gets a green *"…applied at the registrar once it activates"*, and toggles the registrar lock on. Sixty seconds later the domain goes `ACTIVE`. Neither the nameservers nor the lock is ever pushed. The domain stays on name.com's DNS and stays unlocked — and the lock card at `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx:214-217` then prints *"Currently locked (saved — applies once the registrar is connected)"* forever.

---

## 8. `updateNameservers` returns a green "Saved." for a call that touched nothing

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:96` — the registrar call is inside `if (unique.length >= 2)`. Clearing all inputs yields `unique.length === 0`, so the block is skipped entirely: no `setNameservers`, no `note`. Line `:112` writes `nameservers: []` and returns `{ nameservers: [], registrarHit: false, note: undefined }`.

`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:65-69` then falls through to `res.note ?? "Saved."` and renders it in `text-emerald-400` (`:134`).

**Concrete failure:** a customer who previously delegated to Cloudflare wants to revert to name.com's DNS. They clear both fields, click **Save nameservers**, and get a green **"Saved."** The registrar still has the Cloudflare nameservers — permanently. Worse, the form now re-renders with two blank inputs, implying the override is gone. There is no path in the product to undo a nameserver delegation.

---

## 9. WHOIS-privacy toggle never contacts the registrar, and the setup checklist believes it

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152` — `setWhoisPrivacy` does one `db.domain.update`, one audit row, and returns. No `nc(...)` call, unlike its two siblings in the same file (`updateNameservers:99`, `requestTransferOut:186,193`).

The UI presents it as a live control: `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:176-190` is a pill switch with optimistic local flip at `:157`, above copy at `:192-195` describing a real-world effect — *"When on, your personal contact details are hidden from the public WHOIS directory and replaced with privacy-protection contacts"* — and a state readout at `:196-198`. The disclaimer only arrives afterwards, in `res.note`.

**Concrete failure:** registration always sets `privacyEnabled: true` at name.com (`/opt/nxeon/lib/registrar.ts:137`, and `:338` for transfers). A customer registering a **business** domain who wants public WHOIS flips the switch off. The switch goes grey, the DB says `false`, and `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:115` un-ticks *"WHOIS privacy on"* in the Setup checklist, dropping the progress bar. Their contact details are still redacted at name.com. The two states can never be reconciled — nothing reads registrar privacy state back, and `whoisPrivacy` defaults to `true` (`prisma/schema.prisma:209`) for every row regardless of what the registrar did.

---

## 10. The DNS panel is hardcoded to claim name.com is authoritative

`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:243` renders a fixed `<Badge tone="brand">name.com DNS</Badge>`, and `:78` loads records via `getDnsHosts(domain.name)` — name.com's zone API.

`Domain.nameservers` is right there in scope (`:327`) but is never consulted by this panel.

**Concrete failure:** a customer sets custom nameservers via Advanced (which *does* really hit `:setNameservers`, `actions-domains-advanced.ts:99`) and moves DNS to Cloudflare — the same card even warns them *"Setting custom nameservers moves DNS off name.com's servers"* (`DomainAdvanced.tsx:87`). Back on the main page, the DNS records table still lists name.com's now-unauthoritative zone, still badges it `name.com DNS`, and Quick setup / Add record / Import / Reset all still write into that dead zone reporting success. The customer adds an MX record, sees "Added 1", and their mail never routes.

---

## Minor (verified, low impact)

- **`referral_reward_cents` Setting is never read.** Admin-editable at `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/GrowthPanel.tsx:14-17`, whitelisted at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-settings.ts:72`, defaulted at `/opt/nxeon/lib/settings.ts:70`. But `referralRewardCents()` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/growth.ts:13-16`) reads only `process.env.REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS`. Set it to 1000 in admin and `/dashboard/refer` keeps printing `$5.00` (`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx:35, 46, 78`) and keeps crediting $5.00. Contrast `grantSignupCredit`, which correctly uses `getSettingInt(...)` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-growth.ts:234`.
- **`"ISSUING"` is missing from `statusColors`** (`/opt/nxeon/components/ui/primitives.tsx:71-99`), so a certificate mid-issuance renders as the grey `STOPPED` dot on `/dashboard/ssl`. The map's own comment at `:83-87` exists to prevent exactly this fallback.
- **`PointAtServerButton`** (`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DomainControls.tsx:75-110`) is exported and never mounted anywhere — superseded by `DnsQuickSetup`. Dead code, not user-visible.
- **`/dashboard/affiliate` renders money in a currency the platform never charges in.** `formatMoney(..., currency)` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/tax.ts:55-60`) swaps the symbol with **no FX conversion** (documented at `:8-12`). With `currency=EUR`, the affiliate page shows `€25.00` minimum payout and `€12.00 / referral` while `/dashboard/billing` beside it shows `$` via `fmtMoney`. Intentional per the module docs, but the two pages disagree about what the same integer means.

---

## Checked and SOLID

**`Domain.autoRenew` is real** — the specific question asked. `/opt/nxeon/worker/billing.ts:460-582` (`domainAutoRenewSweep`) queries `{ autoRenew: true, status: "ACTIVE", expiresAt: { lt: cutoff } }`, calls `renewDomain` at the registrar, then charges inside a CAS-guarded transaction (`:522-553`) with a PAID invoice, an `AlreadyRenewedError` skip, and an `InsufficientBalanceError` branch that still records the renewal and flags `domain.renew.uncharged` for ops. The toggle at `DomainControls.tsx:14-39` → `actions-domains.ts:373-379` genuinely changes behaviour.

**`Domain.transferStatus` is polled.** `domainTransferInSweep` (`worker/billing.ts:251-309`) refreshes it from the registrar, and `TransferInStatusCard` (`components/customer/DomainTransferIn.tsx:71, 97`) shows the raw registrar string. `transferStatusLabel` (`lib/registrar.ts:413-423`) falls through to the raw value rather than inventing one. Approval nudges are deduped (`worker/billing.ts:367-397`). The card deliberately omits `<AutoRefresh/>` with an honest comment at `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:155-156`.

**`Domain.transferEpp`** — written by `requestTransferOut` (`actions-domains-advanced.ts:210`) and read only as `hasEpp` to relabel the button "Re-reveal" vs "Unlock & reveal" (`page.tsx:329`, `DomainAdvanced.tsx:247`). Small but honest.

**Money paths.** `purchaseDomain`'s dual idempotency + 3-way `verifyRegistration` (`actions-domains.ts:76-90`); `renewDomainAction`'s registrar-expiry adoption and in-tx CAS (`:310-348`); `submitTransferIn`'s registrar-before-wallet ordering with cancel-on-charge-failure (`actions-domains-transfer.ts:206-316`); `cancelTransferIn` crediting only after the registrar confirms (`:370-397`); `settleFailedTransferIn` flipping the original PAID invoice to REFUNDED and scrubbing the auth code (`lib/domain-transfer.ts:97-144`); `requestAffiliatePayout` capping at `min(wallet, unclaimed)` re-read inside the transaction (`actions-affiliate.ts:59-100`); `redeemGiftCode`'s guarded `updateMany` claim (`actions-gift.ts:117-137`).

**DNS mutations are all real and honestly reported.** `addDnsRecord`, `deleteDnsRecord`, `addDnsRecordsBulk`, `importDnsRecords`, `resetDnsToDefaults` every one hits name.com and returns per-record `added` / `skipped` / `failed` with reasons (`lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:132-301`), surfaced faithfully by `ResultBox` (`DnsQuickSetup.tsx:52-77`) including the "Everything was already in place" case. No blanket success anywhere in this file. Redirects and registrar lock **do** call the registrar when the domain is ACTIVE and configured, and return `live: true/false` honestly (`:342-359, 449-467`).

**Billing/invoices.** `invoiceCreateData` derives `amountCents` from line items + tax so the stamped total can't desync (`lib/invoices.ts:72-97`); `invoiceTotals` and the detail page agree; `InvoiceStatusBadge` maps the real Prisma enum with no hardcoding (`InvoiceViews.tsx:4-19`). Notably good: `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:109-117` **hides** `CouponField` when Stripe is configured, precisely because the Stripe path doesn't redeem the cookie — the correct instinct, applied.

**No 404s.** Every link and form target in scope resolves: `/dashboard/domains/{register,transfer,[id]}`, `/dashboard/{refer,affiliate,billing,invoices,invoices/[id],ssl,deploy}`, `/api/domains/check`, `/api/domains/[id]/dns-export`, `/api/invoices/[id]`, `/api/stripe/checkout`. `/dashboard/order` correctly redirects to the existing `/dashboard/deploy`.

**Not re-reported** (your calibration examples): `User.autoRechargeEnabled` / `lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts`, and the migration `status:"DONE"` hardcode.
